claims.note: Title and description are scoped to the verified mechanism: silent front-of-history message loss on /api/chat with prompt_eval_count reporting the clamped size, while the /api/generate head drop is stated as a source reading the probe leaves open. The earlier headline claimed the system prompt never reaches the model; that claim was retracted in rework round 1 because /api/chat re-collects system messages and the codename control failed in every chat cell.

The mechanism paragraph: the 200-with-no-warning behaviour and the metric mismatch are the measured result (see the probe blocks); the claim that front-of-history messages are dropped while system messages are re-collected is read from the v0.20.3 loop, and the /api/generate head question is explicitly left open.

num_ctx wording and the FAQ default are quoted from the current API reference and FAQ; the 4096/32768/262144 tiers are read from the v0.20.3 switch in routes.go. The 'defaults to 2048' claim is attributed to older guides rather than repeated as current.
Function comment, forward loop, system re-collection and the per-iteration renderPrompt call with tools are quoted from server/prompt.go at tag v0.20.3. Code reading, not a live-request inference.

Go block is a verbatim contiguous excerpt of the truncation loop (prompt.go v0.20.3 lines 35-44 after removing tabs); the enclosing condition and fit check were omitted, as the paragraph states. Not reconstructed.

Corrected in rework round 1: main keeps the same loop and stated intent, but the return value is renamed from images []llm.ImageData ('prompt and images') to media []llm.MediaData ('prompt and media'). The earlier 'same comment and the same signature' wording was wrong and is gone.
The silence is the measurement: five responses, all status 200 with no warning field and no error object, plus the documented metric wording. The clamp-is-intended reading is source-level.

run.methodology: Five requests, 2026-10-31 15:24-15:26 UTC, to a local Ollama 0.20.3 daemon at 127.0.0.1:11434 on a 2-vCPU Neoverse-N1 host (11 GB RAM, no GPU) with qwen2.5:0.5b Q4_K_M, temperature 0, num_predict 32, non-streaming. Chat fixture: system message plus twelve padded MSG-nn messages and a final list-the-labels instruction, run once at num_ctx=2048 (control) and twice at num_ctx=512. Generate fixture: one prompt with head sentinel SENTINEL-HEAD-7731 and tail sentinel SENTINEL-TAIL-9917, run at num_ctx=1024 (fits) and num_ctx=256 (overflows). Every request completed; none timed out or was retried. runs.csv stores reply_head truncated to 120 characters; chat-replies.json holds the complete response objects for the two chat cells re-requested at 15:32-15:35 UTC.

claims.note: Model, quantisation, host, sampler settings and fixture shapes are exactly the settings passed by the published driver. One host, so only the shape of the result transfers.

risk_checks.note: Title, description, schema headline and body now describe silent front-of-history message loss on /api/chat plus prompt_eval_count reporting the clamped size; the system-prompt-loss headline was retracted and the codename control failure is published as a negative result in all three chat cells.
The clamp is presented as intended server behaviour whose defect is the missing feedback, not as a regression; no version boundary is asserted.

The /api/generate head-versus-tail question is stated twice as unresolved and the probe is said not to settle it; no measured claim is made about that path. The attribution is to the absence of head protection in the read files, qualified in the review report.

prompt_eval_count is quoted from the chat reference and described as accurate for the evaluated prompt and misleading for the submitted one; the prefill-monitoring page is linked with a boundary caveat rather than contradicted.
Every figure in the table and body traces to runs.csv or chat-replies.json (1032, 465, 45%, 512, 256, 529, 11, 32, 15, wall times) with no cross-host extrapolation.
The 494M-parameter model, the failed control codename and the dropped tail sentinel in the fitting cell are all disclosed as limits on what the probe can establish.

Five first-party files are linked from the article and listed in public_artifacts with hashes matching disk: probe, fixtures, runs.csv, chat-replies.json, chat_replay.py. The quoted replies are backed by retained full response objects, not by the 120-character runs.csv field.

No claim is made that unlisted files are available: method.md and raw-records-manifest.json stay private and are neither linked nor described as published. The raw links use the repository's established evidence path and resolve after the deterministic Publisher commits.

Matches a debugging query ('ollama prompt truncated no error', 'prompt_eval_count wrong'); the piece is a diagnosis with a published probe rather than a ranking, and it links the overlapping API and setup guides instead of repeating them.
No affiliate, sponsorship or paid placement; no vendor recommendation and no hosted-service comparison. No cover image.
Published evidence contains fixture prompts, sentinel strings, response metrics and model replies only; no credentials, absolute host paths, third-party downloads or personal data.
